conviction_note: Mild long. The Q3 revenue guide and the FY guide both excluded Airtable (closed 2026-09-04, ~$480m ARR) and Miro (closed 2026-10-26, ~$600m ARR), so the headline Q3 revenue and the first guide to include them should come in mechanically above the $740-753m Q3 consensus and the ~$2.90bn FY consensus, and BofA (Nov 16) says the buy-side bar has already dropped below guidance. Against that: organic growth slowed from 6% to 3% in Q2, the only prior print fell ~16-17% on a beat, the put skew is +14 vol points with put/call OI at 4.3, and FY27 consensus ($4.26bn) shows the sell-side already models the deals. So p_up is 54 and not higher. The findings sum (+2.5) is above the scaled +1.36 because the mechanical, deal-driven upside is filed at its own size while the scaled number carries how unsure the reaction is on a name that sold its only beat.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue guide $733-745m and adjusted operating income $380-400m, FY2026 revenue $2.78-2.82bn and AOI $1.46-1.51bn, all on the portfolio owned as of 2026-08-12 with no later acquisitions (company Q2 release, https://bendingspoons.com/documents/financials/2026/20260813%20Bending%20Spoons%E2%80%94Q2%202026%20Earnings%20Release%20(6-K%20with%20exhibits).pdf, p.4). Q3 revenue consensus: $740.3m and EPS $0.26 (Earnings Whispers via finviz, 2026-11-15, https://finviz.com/news/422852/bending-spoons-must-bridge-a-full-year-gap-the-street-hasnt-yet-closed), $745.9m and $0.32 (Arincen), $753m (Chartmill, per search snippet). FY2026 revenue consensus $2.88-2.90bn, range $2.8-3.1bn, 12 analysts (finviz 2026-11-15; https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/bsp/forecast/ updated 2026-11-16). FY2027 consensus $4.26bn, so at least some estimates include the deals. BofA, 2026-11-16: buy-side expectations for Q3 revenue and AOI are 'significantly' below guidance (https://finimize.com/content/bofa-thinks-bending-spoons-ai-fears-are-getting-priced-in-early). The Q3 bar is anchored by the company guide; sell-side estimates disagree by about 1.7%; the whisper is below guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 20.14m shares, 6.8 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/bsp). Stock Titan shows a later undated reading of 14.3m shares and 4.2 days (https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/BSP/). That is about 3-6% of float by source, so not a crowded short. Borrow fee about 9.7% per a curvedtrading snippet (page 403, unverified). Baseline: 25-delta skew +14.08 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 4.33, ATM IV 115%, event-implied move 23.9% but ATM spread 31% of mid, so the implied move is noisy. Berkshire Hathaway bought 10m new shares at $33 on 2026-10-14 (stake about 4%) and the stock jumped about 35% that day (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/14/why-bending-spoons-stock-popped-today). Former Miro holders reinvested $295m into about 6.2m shares (about $47.6 each) at the 10-26 close. Spot $42.96: down 5.6% in November, 23% below the 52-week high, run-up +5.6% over 5 days and -6.0% over 20 days. Downgrades: one in the month to 2026-11-18 (AAII); BofA Underperform reiterated 11-16, target $36 raised to $38.

findings.finding: Airtable closed on 2026-09-04 and is consolidated for about 27 days of Q3. At about $480m ARR (June 2026, >20% YoY growth) that is roughly $30-40m of Q3 revenue the $733-745m guide explicitly excluded ('based solely on the portfolio of businesses owned as of August 12, 2026'). Headline Q3 revenue is therefore likely about $770-790m, against a $740-753m consensus, unless analysts already folded it in.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior print: Q2 2026 revenue of $704m beat the $685m consensus by 2.8% and adjusted EPS came in at $0.46 against $0.27, yet the stock fell about 16-17% that day on a full-year guide below consensus (https://finviz.com/news/381910/bending-spoons-shares-slip-despite-q2-earnings-and-revenue-beat). This name has sold its reported-quarter beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Most Q3 consensus figures ($740.3m, $745.9m) sit on the ex-acquisition guide midpoint of $739m. If Airtable were in them they would read about $775m+. Only Chartmill's $753m hints at partial inclusion. A headline beat that is inorganic is usually recognised as such by holders, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: The ARR figure comes from a separate source, the SaaStr deal analysis (https://www.saastr.com/airtable-just-sold-for-2-25b-at-2-7x-arr-it-raised-1-4b-and-was-once-worth-11-7b/), and the guide exclusion from the company's Q2 release p.4. Same deal as the guidance finding below, but a different line (Q3 reported versus the Q4/FY guide).

findings.finding: The Q4/FY outlook given on 11-20 will be the first to include Airtable (a full Q4, roughly $115-125m) and Miro (closed 2026-10-26, about 66 days at about $600m ARR, roughly $100-110m), plus Airtable's September. The FY2026 revenue guide therefore resets mechanically from $2.78-2.82bn to roughly $3.0-3.06bn, above the ~$2.90bn mean consensus whose shortfall drove the Q2 sell-off. On the existing perimeter, the old FY guide implies only about $755m for Q4 (FY $2.80bn less Q1 $601m, Q2 $704m and Q3 $739m), below the ~$840m the street's $2.88-2.90bn implied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY guide is the line this stock traded on last time: a FY revenue midpoint of $2.80bn against $2.895bn consensus sent it down about 16-17% on 2026-08-13 despite the quarterly beat (finviz 381910; https://www.finanzaonline.com/notizie/bending-spoons-deraglia-post-conti-cosa-non-ha-convinto-wall-street).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: FY2027 consensus of $4.26bn (stockanalysis, 2026-11-16) shows models carry the deals forward, and the FY2026 consensus range reaches $3.1bn. But the FY2026 mean is still $2.90bn and the BofA note says the buy-side bar is below guidance, with put skew at +14 and P/C OI at 4.3. If a raised outlook were expected, the put premium would not be this large and the stock would not have fallen 5.6% in November. What decides the sign is the ex-deal Q4: the market sees the headline raise, and the organic core either confirms the ~$755m implied Q4 or beats it.
findings.independence: Airtable timing is from the company completion release (finviz 389082). Miro EV and ARR come from the deal announcement (https://finviz.com/news/390888/bending-spoons-agrees-to-acquire-miro-at-136-billion-enterprise-value). Q1 revenue of $601.3m comes from the F-1 coverage (https://fortune.com/2026/06/08/bending-spoons-italian-aol-evernote-wetransfer-files-us-ipo/). Both deal releases say the company 'expects to incorporate [the business] into its outlook when it next reports financial results'.

findings.finding: Organic revenue growth slowed from 6% in Q1 to 3% in Q2 2026, with Remini and Splice revenue declining and only Tractive and WeTransfer growing (company release). Management cited market saturation and competition at Remini. If the trend continued, Q3 organic growth lands around 0-2%, and the ex-deal Q4 guide implied by the old FY range (~$755m) suggests the core is not re-accelerating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 deceleration from 6% to 3% was cited alongside the FY guide as a cause of the ~16-17% fall on 2026-08-13 (https://www.saastr.com/5-interesting-learnings-from-bending-spoons-at-2-8-billion-in-revenue-126-growth-3-organic-growth-and-1-08-billion-of-arr-bought-in-37-days).
findings.why_not_priced: The deceleration itself is public. What is not known is whether Q3 organic growth turned negative. Organic growth is not a consensus line, and the Airtable and Miro headline will mask it until the release footnote is read. Nobody can trade it ahead of the release, and the put skew is consistent with part of this fear already being in the price.
findings.independence: BofA (2026-11-16) puts about 30% of the revenue run rate as highly exposed to AI disruption, which points the same way (https://finimize.com/content/bofa-thinks-bending-spoons-ai-fears-are-getting-priced-in-early). The WSJ-reported net revenue retention trend was 95% in 2025 and the metric is no longer published (secondary coverage). Net of the rest: Tractive and WeTransfer growing, and repricing at Vimeo, Eventbrite and AOL still being tested, could hold organic growth flat rather than falling.

findings.finding: BofA (Underperform, target raised $36 to $38 on 2026-11-16) wrote that investor expectations for Q3 revenue and adjusted operating income have fallen 'significantly' below management's guidance ($733-745m, $380-400m). The effective buy-side bar sits under the guide, and the company beat its implied guide last quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of a low whisper on this name. Last quarter the reported beat (+2.8% revenue) did not carry the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The note is three days old and its contents are not in wire consensus ($740-753m sits at or above the guide midpoint). A low whisper is by construction positioning that a merely in-line print clears. The heavy put OI and +14 skew are what a below-guide whisper looks like in the options.
findings.independence: The AAII page (2026-11-19) records one downgrade and no upgrades in the prior month and the stock down 5.6% in November (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/552330-why-bending-spoons-spa8217s-bsp-stock-is-up-4128). The bear is the same analyst who reiterated Sell, so the source is not neutral.

findings.finding: Q2 revenue of $704m beat the $685m consensus by 2.8% and adjusted EPS of $0.46 beat $0.27. The Q3 guide implies 113% YoY growth at the midpoint on the August-12 perimeter, and the company has a track record of guiding below what it prints, so Q3 core revenue and AOI likely land at or above the top of $733-745m and $380-400m before Airtable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: That beat was sold, with the stock about -16-17% on 2026-08-13.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits near the guide midpoint, so a repeat top-of-range core print is not in the estimates. It is inference from a single quarter, and the name sold that beat, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: This shares the Q3 guide document with the Airtable finding but is about the organic core, not the deal. The Q2 release's own commentary on AOL, Eventbrite and Vimeo monetization tests supports the core being on track (company release p.4).

findings.finding: Bending Spoons cut a large part of Airtable's team in mid-October 2026 (about 190 roles in one report), the same reorganization playbook it ran at Vimeo, WeTransfer and Tractive. That supports a quick AOI contribution from Airtable in the Q4/2027 outlook, while the severance falls into excluded reorganization expense.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance on this name of an AOI guide that includes a fresh large acquisition.
findings.why_not_priced: The layoffs were public, but the AOI margin Airtable and Miro bring into the Q4 guide has not been quantified anywhere. If it were priced, consensus FY2026 adjusted EPS would not be drifting down (Q3 EPS consensus $0.26 against $0.46 in Q2).
findings.independence: The Q2 release documents the same playbook: $50m of reorganization expense for AOL, Eventbrite, Tractive and Vimeo, with Q2 AOI margin up 5pp to 54%. It is the same entity read as a margin positive, not used both ways.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is skewed to downside: puts carry +14 vol points of 25-delta skew and put/call OI is 4.33. Short interest is 20.1m shares at 6.8 days to cover (2026-09-30), a moderate 3-6% of float. Berkshire Hathaway added 10m shares at $33 on 2026-10-14, about 23% below spot, and a mixed-to-good print meets hedged rather than complacent holders.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-10-14 the Berkshire news moved the stock about +35% in a day, so non-earnings positive news has produced violent upside on this float.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew is itself the price. This finding says only that the downside is paid for, which limits how much a bad print adds relative to an in-line one. It is small because a strong skew is usually right.

findings.finding: Financing: in September, $1.25bn USD and EUR395m euro term loan B add-ons (for Miro), then on 2026-10-28 an upsized ~$1.8bn of senior secured notes due 2032 ($1.25bn at 9.625%, EUR500m at 8.625%, settled about 11-04) for unnamed 'future acquisitions'. That adds roughly $160m a year of interest before any new deal contributes. Pro forma gross debt was $6.64bn and net debt $5.12bn per the 10-20 lender presentation. Asked what the money buys: Miro and Airtable are corroborated, and the rest buys a deal pipeline the company says runs at about five a year, with no named target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose into late October across the notes announcement (+36.6% over the month to 10-30, mostly Berkshire), so the market did not punish the debt at the time.
findings.why_not_priced: The coupon is public. The Q4 interest line and the adjusted-EPS guide (Q3 EPS consensus has fallen to $0.26) show it, and the first EPS outlook carrying the notes lands on 11-20. Mostly priced, so sized small.
findings.independence: Leverage and presentation figures: https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/bending-spoons-raccoglie-1-5-mld-2722222 (2026-10-28). CEO: 'we would prefer to pay less' but returns exceed the cost (https://www.soldionline.it/notizie/mercati-esteri/bending-spoons-e-il-debito-perche-ferrari-dice-che-il-costo-e-razionale, 2026-10-29).

outside_window.finding: The IPO lock-up of about 180 days from the 2026-07-01 pricing expires around 2026-12-28. Lock-up terms and any earnings-linked early release were not found in public sources.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly long through the mechanical guide reset and a sub-guide whisper. That cuts against a +14 put skew, put/call OI of 4.3 and the stock's only prior print (-16% on a beat). So p_up is held at 54, and the stated reason the options may be wrong is that the first outlook including more than $1bn of acquired ARR rebases the FY number above the consensus whose shortfall caused the last sell-off.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its only beat, -16%): Airtable headline-revenue finding cut 1.0 -> 0.5; organic-beat finding cut 0.5 -> 0.3; p_up 55 -> 54.
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong +14 skew needs an explicit reason or a smaller size): guidance-reset finding cut 2.0 -> 1.5, with the reason stated in baseline_tension.
Lesson 5/9 (inference from the Q2 trend, net of the growing Tractive and WeTransfer): organic-deceleration negative cut -2.0 -> -1.5.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): use corroborated (Miro, Airtable, stated deal cadence), so the notes finding shrinks -0.5 -> -0.3 and keeps only the interest-expense drag.
Lesson 6 (bar and window): the bar is sourced to the company guide with consensus spread noted; the lock-up stays in outside_window; nothing else changed.
